titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§281–282: Ögödei’s four deeds and four faults
part: §§281–282 — Ögödei’s four deeds and four faults
about: The last two sections. Ögödei Qahan reckons up his reign in his own words: four deeds he added to his father’s work — the conquest of the Jurchen, the post-roads, wells in waterless land, watchmen in the towns — and four faults: wine, the girls of his uncle Ödchigin’s people, the secret harming of the loyal Doqolqu, and walling in the wild game against his brothers. §282 is the colophon: the book was written and finished while the great assembly was gathered on the Kerülen, in the seventh month of a Rat year.

sentences.t: Ögödei Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Ögödei Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: Ögödei Qahan said:
sentences.n: Ügülerün is ügüle- “speak” with the converb of time -rün, “saying” (Ming 說), the text’s usual way of bringing in a speech. Shiratori opens the quotation at the next word, Ečige-jüġen; the speech runs to the end of §281 and closes at bolžuγ̇ui-že.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, Chinggis’s son and successor as Qahan [(人)名, “a man’s name”]
converb of time: “saying, as he spoke”

sentences.t: "Ečige-jüġen jeke oron-dur saγ̇užu qaγan ečige-jin qoina üiledügsen min-u
sentences.l: "One’s-own-father great throne-on sitting, Qaγan father’s after, having-done my:
sentences.i: “Since I sat on my father’s great throne, these are the things I have done after the Qahan my father:
sentences.n: Ečige-jüġen is ečige “father” + the reflexive-possessive -jüġen, “one’s own father” (Ming 父 自的行); it points back to the speaker, so “my father”. Oron-dur takes the dative-locative -dur, back-vowel form (Ming 位 裏, “in the seat”). Qoina “after” follows the genitive ečige-jin (Ming 父的 後). Üiledügsen is the past participle of üiled- “do” (Ming 做了的), and min-u after it is its subject in the genitive, “my having done”: the phrase is a heading, and the deeds follow. “These are the things” is supplied in `i`.

morph.gloss: past participle: “having done; what was done” [了的]

sentences.t: Žaγud-un irgen-dür ajalažu Žaγud irgen muqudγaba bi.
sentences.l: Žaγud’s people-to campaigning, Žaγud people destroyed I.
sentences.i: I marched against the Jurchen people and brought the Jurchen people to an end.
sentences.n: First deed. Žaγud is the Jurchen of the Jin state (Ming 金人). Irgen-dür is the dative-locative (front-vowel -dür, after the front vowels of irgen), the target of ajala- “campaign against” (Ming 征進着). Muqudγaba (Ming 窮絕了, “exhausted and ended”) is a past in -ba; the stem is taken as one word muqudγa- “bring to an end”, but how it is built is not certain. Bi “I” stands after the verb, as often in this speech.

morph.gloss: the Jurchen, the people of the Jin state [金人]
to bring to an end, destroy (stem analysis not certain) [窮絕]

sentences.t: Nögöġe üile min-u elčin bidan-u žaγ̇ura öterlen qaγ̇ulqui.
sentences.l: Second deed my: envoys our between quickly running.
sentences.i: My second deed: that envoys should run swiftly along our ways.
sentences.n: No finite verb: qaγ̇ulqui is a verbal noun, “the running” (Ming 走的), so the sentence is a heading, “the envoys’ running”. Bidan-u is the inclusive “our” (Ming 咱的), genitive of bida. Žaγ̇ura “between, in the interval” is glossed 路間, “on the roads between”. Öterlen is a modal converb in -n, “hastening” (Ming 快). Min-u may go with üile (“my second deed”) or with elčin (“my envoys”); the Ming 我的 does not decide.

morph.gloss: between, in the interval; here “along the ways” [路間]

sentences.t: Basa kereg žereg(i)-jen žüġeġülküj-e žamud tabiγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Again, needs one’s-own-requirements for-causing-to-carry, post-stations caused-to-set.
sentences.i: Again, I had post-stations set up to carry what was needed.
sentences.n: Žüġeġülküj-e is a stack: žüġe- “carry” (Ming 搬運) + causative -ġül- (Ming 敎) + verbal noun -küi + dative-locative -e (Ming 行), “for having (things) carried”. Kereg žereg(i)-jen pairs two words for “need” (Ming 所用 需); -(i)jen is the reflexive-possessive, “their own needs” (Ming 自的行). Shiratori prints tabiγ̇ulba, but the Han 塔勒必兀勒罷 writes the l, talbiγ̇ulba (as at talbižu below): talbi- “set” + causative -γ̇ul- + past -ba (Ming 敎放了). Žamud is the plural of žam “road, post-station” (Ming 站每).

morph.gloss: need, matter, what is used [所用]
reflexive-possessive, with accusative (i): one’s own [自的行]
to set, place, establish (printed tabi-; the Han 塔勒必 writes talbi-) [放]

sentences.t: Basa nögöġe üile usu ügei γažar-a quduγ̇ud eriġülžü γarγaγ̇ulžu ulus irgen usun ebesün-e kürgeġülbe.
sentences.l: Again, next deed: water-without land-in wells causing-to-dig, causing-to-bring-out, nation people water grass-to caused-to-reach.
sentences.i: Again, the next deed: in waterless land I had wells dug and brought forth, and brought the people of the realm to water and grass.
sentences.n: Two converbs in -žü/-žu, then the finite verb: front-vowel eriġülžü beside back-vowel γarγaγ̇ulžu, vowel harmony at work. Both carry the causative -ġül-/-γ̇ul- (Ming 敎): “causing to dig, causing to bring out” (Ming 敎掘着 敎出着). Γarγaγ̇ulžu and kürgeġülbe have two causatives each: γar- “go out” → γarγa- “bring out” → γarγaγ̇ul- “have brought out”; kür- “reach” → kürge- “bring to” → kürgeġül- “have brought to” (Ming 敎到了). Usu ügei γažar-a “in land without water” (Ming 水 無 地行). Ulus irgen “nation, people” is a pair (Ming 國 百姓); usun ebesün-e “to water and grass”, that is, pasture.

sentences.t: Basa žüg žüg balaγad-un irgen-dür alginči tanmačin talbižu
sentences.l: Again, every-quarter towns’ people-among watchmen tanmačin setting,
sentences.i: Again, I set watchmen and tanmachin among the people of the towns on every side,
sentences.n: The converb chain of this sentence is broken in two here. Žüg žüg, doubled, is distributive, “every quarter” (Ming 各處 各處). Balaγad-un “of the towns” (Ming 城(每)的). Alginči is glossed 哨望的, “one who keeps watch”; tanmačin only 官名, “a title of office”, so it is left as it stands. Talbižu “setting” (Ming 放着): the converb here keeps back-vowel -žu after the stem’s final i.

morph.gloss: direction, side, quarter; doubled, “every quarter” [各處]
tanmachin, a kind of officer or garrison post; the Ming gives only “title of office” [官名]

sentences.t: ulus irgen-ü köl köser-e γar γažar-a talbiγ̇ulžu aγ̇ulba bi.
sentences.l: nation people’s foot earth-on, hand ground-on causing-to-set, caused-to-dwell I.
sentences.i: and let the people of the realm set foot on the earth and hand on the ground, and live in rest.
sentences.n: Continues the chain. Köl köser-e γar γažar-a “foot on the earth, hand on the ground” (Ming 腳 地行 手 地行) is an image of settled ease; both nouns take the dative-locative -e/-a. Talbiγ̇ulžu “causing to set” (Ming 敎放着). Aγ̇ulba is glossed 住了, “stayed, dwelt”: taken as a- “be, dwell” + causative -γ̇ul-, “I caused (them) to dwell”, but the Ming has no 敎 here and the reading is not certain; “in rest” in `i` is an interpretation.

morph.gloss: causative: let … dwell (doubtful; the Ming has no 敎)

sentences.t: Qaγan ečige-jüġen qoina dörben üiles nemebe-že
sentences.l: Qaγan one’s-own-father after four deeds added indeed
sentences.i: After the Qahan my father, I have added four deeds.
sentences.n: Ečige-jüġen again “one’s own father” (Ming 父 自的行); qoina “after” (Ming 後). Dörben üiles “four deeds” (Ming 四件 勾當(每)); üiles is üile + plural -s. Nemebe-že is neme- “add” + past -be + the particle -že, which the Ming writes 也者, an emphatic “so it is”. Shiratori puts no stop here, but the next word is capitalised; the unit closes at the sentence.

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, so it is [也者]

sentences.t: Basa Qaγan ečige-deġen jeke oro ba saγ̇uldažu olon ulus(i)-jan deġere min-u ačižu odtažu
sentences.l: Again, Qaγan at-one’s-own-father’s great throne also being-made-to-sit, many one’s-own-people upon my loading, being-gone,
sentences.i: Again: set on the great throne of the Qahan my father, bearing my many people upon me, I was carried away,
sentences.n: Now the faults, the long first sentence cut in two. Ečige-deġen is the reflexive-possessive in the dative-locative, “at one’s own father’s” (Ming 父 自的行). Saγ̇uldažu is saγ̇u- “sit” + causative -ul- + passive -da- + converb -žu, “being made to sit” (Ming 敎坐着). Ulus(i)-jan “one’s own people” (Ming 百姓 自的行), back-vowel -jan; deġere min-u “upon me” (Ming 上 我的). Odtažu is glossed 被去着, “being gone”: od- “go” + passive -ta-. What it means here is not clear: “carried off, carried away” is a guess.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive dative-locative: at one’s own (front-vowel form) [自的行]
reflexive-possessive, with accusative (i): one’s own (back-vowel form) [自的行]

sentences.t: böġed bor darasun-a ilaγdaqu min-u buruγ̇u bolba.
sentences.l: then grape wine-by being-conquered my fault became.
sentences.i: and then to be overcome by grape wine — this was my fault.
sentences.n: Ilaγdaqu is ilaγ- “conquer” + passive -da- + verbal noun -qu, “being conquered” (Ming 被勝了); the agent of the passive stands in the dative-locative, darasun-a “by the wine” (Ming 酒行). Bor is glossed 葡萄酒 “grape wine”, darasun 酒 “wine”. Böġed “then, and so” (Ming 便).

morph.gloss: dative-locative: here the agent of the passive, “by” [行]

sentences.t: Nigen buruγ̇u min-u ene bolba-že.
sentences.l: One fault my this became indeed.
sentences.i: This was one fault of mine.
sentences.n: Bolba-že: past -ba + the emphatic -že (Ming 做了 也者). Nigen “one” is glossed 一件, “one item”: he is counting.

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, so it is [也者]

sentences.t: Nögöġe buruγ̇u josu ügei eme küġün-ü üge-dür orožu
sentences.l: Second fault: reason-without woman person’s word-into entering,
sentences.i: The second fault: giving way, without right, to a woman’s words,
sentences.n: The sentence is cut at the converb. Josu ügei “without right, without reason” (Ming 理 無). Eme küġün “woman person” is a woman (Ming 婦 人); küġün-ü genitive. Üge-dür orožu “entering into (her) word” (Ming 言語 裏 入着): to go by what she said.

sentences.t: Ödčigin abaγa-jin ulus-un ökid abčiraγ̇ulqu alžiγ̇as bolba-že.
sentences.l: Ödčigin uncle’s nation’s girls causing-to-bring errors became indeed.
sentences.i: I had the girls of my uncle Ödchigin’s people brought: these were errors.
sentences.n: Abaγa “father’s younger brother” (Ming 叔叔); Ödchigin is Chinggis’s youngest brother. Ökid is the plural of ökin “girl” (Ming 女子每), the n replaced by -d. Abčiraγ̇ulqu is abčira- “bring” + causative -γ̇ul- + verbal noun -qu, “having (them) brought” (Ming 敎將來的). Alžiγ̇as “errors” is plural (Ming 差每).

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, so it is [也者]

sentences.t: Ulus-un ežen qaγan böġetele josu ügei alžiγ̇as üile-dür dölesgekü min-u nigen buruγ̇u ene bolba-že.
sentences.l: Nation’s lord Qaγan being-while, reason-without errors deed-in being-caught-up my one fault this became indeed.
sentences.i: That I, while lord of the realm and Qahan, was caught up in wrongful, mistaken deeds — this was one fault.
sentences.n: Böġetele is the terminative converb, “while (I) was” (Ming 有間). Dölesgekü is glossed 趂閧的, roughly “joining in a commotion, going along with the crowd”; the verb is not met elsewhere in the part and its exact sense is not certain. Min-u is again the subject of the verbal noun in the genitive: “my being caught up”.

morph.gloss: to be caught up in, join in a commotion (meaning not certain) [趂閧]
emphatic particle: indeed, so it is [也者]

sentences.t: Basa Doqolqu-ji kegesülekü nigen buruγ̇u.
sentences.l: Again, Doqolqu-(obj) secretly-harming one fault.
sentences.i: Again, the secret harming of Doqolqu was one fault.
sentences.n: Doqolqu-ji: -ji is the accusative after a vowel; the Ming writes it 行, as it does the accusative on küġün-i below. Kegesülekü is a verbal noun, “harming in secret” (Ming 陰害的). This is probably Doqolqu the cherbi of §§227–229, but the text does not say. No verb: the clause is a list item.

morph.gloss: accusative (the form used after a vowel) [行]

sentences.t: Ker buruγ̇u kēġesü qān ečige-jin min-u tus-u-γ̇an emüne ölümlekü Doqolqu-ji kegesülekü buruγ̇u alžiγ̇as.
sentences.l: How fault if-saying: Qān father’s my one’s-own-true-lord before pressing-forward Doqolqu-(obj) secretly-harming fault error.
sentences.i: If one asks why it was a fault: to harm in secret Doqolqu, who pressed forward before his own true lord, the Qan my father — that was a fault and an error.
sentences.n: Kēġesü is keġe- “say” + conditional -sü, “if (one) says” (Ming 說呵); ker buruγ̇u “how a fault” (Ming 怎生 不是). Qān is the contracted form of qaγan (Ming 皇帝). Tus-u-γ̇an is glossed 正主自的行, “one’s own true lord”: tus “proper, true” with the reflexive-possessive -γ̇an; the -u- between them is not clear. Ölümlekü “who pressed forward, exerted himself” (Ming 向前的).

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (contracted form of qaγan) [皇帝]
proper, true; here “one’s true lord” [正主]
to press forward, exert oneself [向前]
accusative (the form used after a vowel) [行]

sentences.t: Edöġe min-u emüne ken tein ülümležü öġkü.
sentences.l: Now my before who so pressing-forward will-give.
sentences.i: Now who will press forward so, before me?
sentences.n: Ken “who” (Ming 誰) makes this a question without a question particle. Ülümležü is the same verb as ölümlekü, printed here with ü- (Ming 向前着). Öġkü “will give” (Ming 與的), after a converb, means “do it for (me)”.

morph.gloss: to press forward (printed here with ü-) [向前]
to give; after a converb, “do for (someone)” [與]

sentences.t: Qaγan ečige-jin min-u bürin-ü emüne töre kičijekü küġün-i ülü uqan öisüledügse- n(i)-jen öġer(i)-jen buruγ̇ušijaba bi.
sentences.l: Qaγan father’s my all’s before law diligent person-(obj) not discerning, secretly-harmed-having-one’s-own, self-one’s-own declared-wrong I.
sentences.i: The man who, before us all, kept diligently to the law of the Qahan my father — him I harmed in secret, not understanding; I hold myself at fault.
sentences.n: Küġün-i “the man” (Ming 人行) carries the accusative -i and is the object of öisüledügse-n(i)-jen; the participle kičijekü “diligent” (Ming 謹︀愼的) and töre “law, the right way” (Ming 道理) describe him. Ülü uqan “not understanding” (Ming 不 省): ülü negates the verb. Shiratori splits öisüledügsen(i)-jen over a line: öisüle- “harm in secret” (Ming 陰害, the same gloss as kegesüle- above) + past participle -dügsen + reflexive -(i)jen, “my own having harmed”. Öġer(i)-jen “myself” (Ming 自己). Buruγ̇ušijaba is buruγ̇u “wrong” + -šija- “declare” + past -ba, “declared wrong” (Ming 說不是了).

morph.gloss: law, order, the right way [道理]
past participle; its final n is printed with the next word [了的]
final n of the participle -dügsen, carried over in print
reflexive-possessive, with accusative (i): one’s own [自的行]
reflexive-possessive, with accusative (i): one’s own [自的行]

sentences.t: Basa teṅgeri γažar-ača žajaγ̇atu töregsen göreġesün-i aqa deġü žüg oduγ̇uži keġen
sentences.l: Again, Heaven earth-from destiny-having born wild-beasts-(obj), elder younger-brother side lest-going saying,
sentences.i: Again, fearing that the wild beasts, born with a destiny from Heaven and Earth, might go over to the side of my elder and younger brothers,
sentences.n: The last fault is one long converb chain, cut here into three. Γažar-ača is the ablative, “from” (Ming 地行); žajaγ̇atu is žajaγ̇a “destiny” + possessive -tu, “destiny-having” (Ming 命 有的), the phrase used of the first ancestor in §1. Oduγ̇uži is od- “go” + the dubitative -uγ̇uži, “lest (they) go” (Ming 恐去), and keġen “saying, thinking” (Ming 麽道) closes the thought. Göreġesün-i takes the accusative because the beasts are also the object of qaramlažu in the next unit.

sentences.t: qaramlažu quruγ̇a joγ̇urγa noduγ̇lžu žedgüžü aqu bolun
sentences.l: grudging, stockade wall causing-to-build, holding-back, living being,
sentences.i: I grudged them, and had stockades and walls built to hold them in; and as I lived so,
sentences.n: Qaramlažu “grudging, being greedy” (Ming 貪着). Quruγ̇a joγ̇urγa “stockade, wall” (Ming 寨 墻). Shiratori prints noduγ̇lžu; the Han 那都兀勒周 writes -γ̇ul-, the causative, “causing to build” (Ming 敎築着); the stem is uncertain. Žedgüžü “blocking” (Ming 當着), front-vowel -žü. Aqu bolun (Ming 住 做) is taken as “being one who lives (so)”; the exact force is not certain.

morph.gloss: causative, printed -γ̇l- (the Han 兀勒 writes -γ̇ul-) [敎]

sentences.t: aqa deġü-dēče čimaliγai üge sonosba bi.
sentences.l: elder younger-brother-from resentment word heard I.
sentences.i: I heard words of resentment from my elder and younger brothers.
sentences.n: Deġü-dēče is the ablative, “from” (Ming 行), printed with long ē; aqa deġü “elder and younger brothers” share it. Čimaliγai “resentment, complaint” (Ming 怨).

sentences.t: Buruγ̇u kü bolba.
sentences.l: Fault too became.
sentences.i: That too was a fault.
sentences.n: Kü is an emphatic particle (Ming 也): “that also”.

sentences.t: Qaγan ečige-jüġen qoina dörben üiles nemebe-že bi.
sentences.l: Qaγan one’s-own-father after four deeds added indeed I.
sentences.i: After the Qahan my father I have added four deeds;
sentences.n: A restatement of the earlier sentence, now with bi “I” at the end.

morph.gloss: emphatic particle: indeed, so it is [也者]

sentences.t: Dörben üiles buruγ̇u bolžuγ̇ui-že" keġebe.
sentences.l: Four deeds fault became indeed" said.
sentences.i: and four of my deeds have been faults.” So he spoke.
sentences.n: Bolžuγ̇ui is bol- “become” + the past -žuγ̇ui (Ming 做了), a past of what has turned out so; with -že (Ming 也者). Shiratori closes the quotation here; keġebe “said” (Ming 說了) is the narrator’s. With this the narrative of the Secret History ends.

morph.gloss: past of what has turned out so [了]

sentences.t: Jeke qurilta qurižu quluγana žil huran sara-da
sentences.l: Great assembly assembling, Rat year seventh month-in,
sentences.i: When the great assembly had gathered, in the seventh month of the Rat year,
sentences.n: The colophon. Qurilta “assembly” (Ming 聚會) and qurižu “assembling” (Ming 聚着) are from the same stem quri- “gather”. Quluγana žil “Rat year” (Ming 鼠兒 年). Huran is glossed 七 “seven”, but it is not the ordinary numeral doloγ̇an, which follows a few words on with the same gloss; it may be the month’s own name, and that is not certain. Sara-da “in the month” (Ming 月 行): -da, the dative-locative after a vowel.

morph.gloss: assembly, the gathering of princes and officers [聚會]
seven(th) — so the Ming; not the ordinary numeral doloγ̇an [七]

sentences.t: Kelüren-ü Ködeġe-Aral-un doloγ̇an boldaγ-a Silginčeg qojar žaγ̇ura ordos baγ̇užu büküi-dür bičižü daγ̇usba.
sentences.l: Kelüren’s Ködeġe-Aral’s seven solitary-hill-at, Silginčeg two between, palaces camping being-at-time, writing finished.
sentences.i: while the palaces were encamped at Köde’ü-Aral on the Kerülen, between the two, the Seven Lone Hills and Silgincheg, the writing was completed.
sentences.n: Two genitives in a row, Kelüren-ü Ködeġe-Aral-un, “the Kerülen’s Köde’ü-Aral’s” (Ming 河名的 地名的); Shiratori prints Ködeġe- here, and the house spelling Köde’ü-Aral is kept. Doloγ̇an boldaγ-a is glossed 七 孤山 行, “at the seven solitary hills”: the Ming translates it, so `i` does too, though it may be a place name. Qojar žaγ̇ura “between the two” (Ming 兩 間). Ordos is the plural of ordo, the ruler’s palace-tents (Ming 宮(每)). Büküi-dür “at the time of being” (Ming 有時) is bü- “be” + verbal noun -küi + dative-locative -dür. Bičižü daγ̇usba “writing, finished” (Ming 寫着 畢了): who wrote is not said.

morph.gloss: Köde’ü-Aral, a place on the Kerülen [地名]
